items.description: Fergana is a city in eastern Uzbekistan, serving as the administrative center of Fergana Region. It is a major industrial hub in the Fergana Valley.
facts: Known for oil refining and textile industries.
Located in the fertile Fergana Valley.

items.description: Shahrisabz is a city in southern Uzbekistan, famous as the birthplace of the 14th-century Turco-Mongol conqueror Timur. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
facts: Historic Center is a UNESCO site.

items.description: Zarafshan is a city in the Navoiy Region of Uzbekistan, known for its gold mining industry. It is often referred to as the 'Gold Capital of Uzbekistan'.
facts: Built in the 1960s for gold mining.
Produces a significant amount of gold.

items.description: Yangiyul is a city in the Tashkent Region of Uzbekistan. It is an industrial center with a focus on food processing and construction materials.
Khodjeyli is a city in the Republic of Karakalpakstan, Uzbekistan, situated on the Amu Darya river. It is an ancient settlement with historical significance.
facts: Located on the Amu Darya river.
Served as a trade center in ancient times.

items.description: Chor Minor is a historic madrasah in the city of Bukhara, Uzbekistan, famous for its four minarets. It was built in the early 19th century.
facts: Part of the historic center of Bukhara.

items.description: The Kok Gumbaz Mosque is a prominent historical monument in Shahrisabz, Uzbekistan, part of the Dorut Tilovat Complex. It features a large blue dome.
The Minor Mosque is a modern mosque in Tashkent, Uzbekistan, known for its white marble and intricate decorations. It opened in 2014.
The Sitorai Mokhi-Khosa Palace is the former summer residence of the last Emir of Bukhara, located near Bukhara, Uzbekistan. It blends Eastern and European architectural styles.
Siyob Bazaar is the largest and oldest market in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, located adjacent to the Bibi-Khanym Mosque. It is a vibrant central point for local trade.
facts: Sells fresh produce, spices, and crafts.

items.description: The Afrosiyob Museum of Samarkand is dedicated to the history of the ancient city of Afrosiyob, the predecessor of modern Samarkand. It houses artifacts from various archaeological excavations.
Kalta Minor is a distinctive turquoise-tiled minaret in Khiva, Uzbekistan, notable for its unfinished height. It was intended to be the tallest minaret in Central Asia.
facts: Famous for its blue and green tiles.

items.description: Tash-Hauli Palace is a historical palace complex in Khiva, Uzbekistan, built in the 19th century as the main residence of the Khiva Khans. It is known for its exquisite courtyards and intricate tilework.
The Savitsky Art Museum, also known as the State Museum of Art of Karakalpakstan, is located in Nukus, Uzbekistan. It houses a unique collection of Russian avant-garde art.
facts: Houses a major Russian avant-garde collection.

items.description: The Kyzylkum Desert is the 15th largest desert in the world, spanning parts of Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, and Turkmenistan. Its name means 'Red Sands' in Turkic.
